data.name: Hemant
data.gender_notes: Hemant is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Sanskrit word ‘हेमन्त’ (Hemant), derived from ‘हेम’ (Hem) meaning ‘sun’ and ‘न्त’ (nt) meaning ‘brilliance’. It is a name associated with the brilliance and splendor of the sun. The name Hemant carries the meaning “Sun's brilliance” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Hemant usually hope their child will grow to embody sun's brilliance and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Hemant belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Sun's brilliance.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hemant total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Hemant is of great cultural significance in Hindu traditions. In Hindu mythology, the sun is considered a source of life, light, and energy. The sun god Surya deva is an integral part of various Hindu rituals and ceremonies. The name Hemant is inspired by the brilliance and magnificent presence of the sun. It is also a name that signifies the arrival of autumn in India, a season associated with the harvest and new beginnings.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the name Hemant represents the inner brilliance and light that resides within every individual. It is a reminder to let our inner light shine bright and illuminate our path in life. The name also signifies the connection between the individual soul and the divine, representing the journey towards self-realization and enlightenment. The name Hemant encourages one to awaken their inner sun and radiate positivity and light into the world.

historical_references.reference: Hemant is a Sanskrit word meaning 'sunlight' or 'warm', and is a common name in India. It is derived from the root word 'hem' which means 'sun'. This name was popular during the medieval period (11th to 16th centuries) in various parts of India, especially in regions with a warm climate.
historical_references.context: Derivation and popularity during the medieval period in India

historical_references.reference: The Hindu lunisolar calendar divides the year into six seasons, each lasting approximately two months. Hemant Ritu, or the Hemant season, is the season of autumn, particularly in North India. It is preceded by Sharad Ritu (autumn harvest season) and succeeded by Shishir Ritu (winter). This season is marked by cool and dry weather, and is considered an ideal time for various religious and cultural activities such as marriage ceremonies, Karthik Purnima, and Diwali.
historical_references.context: Hemant season in Hindu lunisolar calendar
